payload.name: Saturate-search-before-answering-ownership-counts
payload.description: Use when a question asks how many items a person owns/has and the first search returns some named item instances; do not stop before all distinct instances are found.
content: When counting items a person owns/has, treat any single retrieval as partial evidence: it often names only some of the person's items while other acquisition/ownership memories exist separately.

Before answering, issue follow-up searches with acquisition/ownership verbs (adopted, bought, received, got, owns) and the names of items already found, plus singular/plural object forms, until consecutive searches surface no new distinct item instance.
Pool evidence across all retrieved memories before finalizing: enumerate every distinct named item attributed to the person, and only sum them after search saturation confirms the set is complete.

solves: When counting items a person owns/has, a single retrieval often returns only a subset of the owned instances; separate acquisition memories for other items exist but are missed because the agent stops after the first partial count. This rule forces iterative, saturation-based searching using acquisition verbs and the names of already-found items before summing, and applies to any future 'how many X does Y own/have' question.
